lessons.title: 主谓句1：动词谓语句
lessons.explanation: The basic sentence: a subject followed by a verb and an optional object.

examples.chinese: 我吃米饭。
examples.english: I eat rice.

allset.title: Basic sentence order
allset.note: In its most basic form, Chinese word order is very similar to English word order. These similarities definitely have their limits, though; don't expect the two languages' word orders to stay consistent much beyond the very basic sentence orders outlined below.

lessons.title: “是”字句1（等同或类属）
lessons.explanation: 是 links the subject to what it equals or what category it belongs to.

examples.chinese: 我是学生。
examples.english: I am a student.

lessons.title: “有”字句1（领有）
lessons.explanation: 有 expresses possession: the subject has something.

examples.chinese: 我有一个姐姐。
examples.english: I have an older sister.

examples.chinese: 我有钱。
examples.english: I have money.

examples.chinese: 你有房子吗？
examples.english: Do you have a house?

allset.title: Expressing possession with "you"
allset.note: 有 (yǒu) can be used in various ways, but the most basic meaning of this verb you need to know is "to have."

lessons.title: 否定副词“不”
lessons.explanation: 不 before a verb or adjective negates present, habitual, or intended actions and states.

examples.chinese: 我不是老师。
examples.english: I am not a teacher.

examples.chinese: 他们不是坏孩子。
examples.english: They are not bad kids.

examples.chinese: 我们不喝酒。
examples.english: We don't drink alcohol.

allset.title: Standard negation with "bu"
allset.note: 不 (bù) is generally used to negate a verb in the present or future, or to talk about what you do not do, as a habit. So expressing things like "I don't want to go" or "I'm not going" or "I don't eat meat" would be typical uses of 不 (bù).

lessons.title: 否定副词“没（有）”
lessons.explanation: 没(有) negates possession and completed actions: “not have / did not”.

examples.chinese: 我没有钱。
examples.english: I have no money.

examples.chinese: 我没有去上班。
examples.english: I didn't go to work.

examples.chinese: 他们没有说话。
examples.english: They didn't speak.

allset.title: Negation of past actions with "meiyou"
allset.note: Use 没有 (méiyǒu) to negate past actions (to say that someone didn't do something, or something didn't happen).

lessons.title: 语气助词“吗”
lessons.explanation: Sentence-final 吗 turns a statement into a yes-no question.

examples.chinese: 你是学生吗？
examples.english: Are you a student?

examples.chinese: 你喜欢咖啡 。
examples.english: You like coffee.

examples.chinese: 你喜欢咖啡吗 ？
examples.english: Do you like coffee?

allset.title: Yes-no questions with "ma"
allset.note: The question particle 吗 (ma) is a simple way to form questions in Chinese. By placing 吗 (ma) on the end of a statement, you convert it into a yes/no question (questions that could be answered with "yes" or "no" in English).

lessons.title: 疑问代词（什么、谁、哪儿、几、多少……）
lessons.explanation: Question words like 什么, 谁, 哪儿 stand in the sentence position of the thing being asked about.

examples.chinese: 这是什么？
examples.english: What is this?

examples.chinese: 什么
examples.english: what

examples.chinese: 哪里 、 哪儿
examples.english: where

allset.title: Placement of question words
allset.note: Who, what, when, where, why, and how: these question words are all used when forming questions in Chinese. The important thing to remember is that word order is the same in Chinese for questions and statements.

lessons.title: 正反问句
lessons.explanation: A yes-no question formed by juxtaposing the positive and negative forms of the verb or adjective.

examples.chinese: 你去不去？
examples.english: Are you going or not?

examples.chinese: 是不是 ？
examples.english: Is it (or not)?

examples.chinese: 他们来不来 ？
examples.english: Are they going to come or not?

allset.title: Affirmative-negative question
allset.note: A common way to form questions in Chinese is to first use a verb in the positive, then repeat the same verb in its negative form, similar to how in English we can say, "Do you have money or not?" or "Have you or have you not been to the park?" This sentence pattern feels a lot more natural in Chinese than those admittedly awkward English equivalents, however.

lessons.title: 结构助词“的”
lessons.explanation: The particle 的 links a modifier to its noun and marks possession: 我的书 “my book”.

examples.chinese: 那是我的书。
examples.english: That is my book.

examples.chinese: 我的老师
examples.english: my teacher

examples.chinese: 你的手机
examples.english: your cell phone

allset.title: Expressing possession with "de"
allset.note: In Chinese, possession is marked with the particle 的 (de), placed after the "owner" noun or noun phrase. This particle works in a similar way to apostrophe-"s" in English, but is used much more broadly in Chinese. This article highlights one of its simplest and most common usages.

lessons.title: 名量词（本、个、家、口、块、件、只、元；杯）
lessons.explanation: A measure word must stand between a number or demonstrative and its noun; 个 is the most general one.

examples.chinese: 我买了三个苹果。
examples.english: I bought three apples.

examples.chinese: 一个人
examples.english: a person

examples.chinese: 两只猫
examples.english: two cats

allset.title: Measure words for counting
allset.note: Chinese uses measure words, a type of word called classifiers in linguistics which are common in East Asian languages. Measure words have a number of important uses, but one of the first ways you'll need to use them is for counting. Chinese learners should master them, starting with the measure word 个 (gè).

lessons.title: 主谓句2：形容词谓语句
lessons.explanation: An adjective serves directly as the predicate: no 是 is used before it.

examples.chinese: 爸爸今天很忙。
examples.english: Dad is very busy today.

examples.chinese: 我很好。
examples.english: I'm good.

examples.chinese: 你很漂亮。
examples.english: You are pretty.

allset.title: Simple "noun + adjective" sentences
allset.note: In English, nouns can be "linked" to adjectives and other nouns with the verb "to be." In Chinese, nouns are linked to other nouns in one way, but linked to adjectives in a completely different way. Nouns are linked to other nouns with 是 (shì). Nouns are linked to adjectives with 很 (hěn).

lessons.title: 时间表示法
lessons.explanation: Clock time is stated with 点 for the hour and 分 for the minutes, placed before the verb.

examples.chinese: 现在三点十分。
examples.english: It is now ten past three.

examples.chinese: 九点
examples.english: 9 o'clock

examples.chinese: 上午七点
examples.english: 7 o'clock a.m.

allset.title: Structure of times (basic)
allset.note: Time in Chinese, just like in English, is expressed by stating the hour first, and then the minute (big to small).

lessons.title: 前缀“小-”
lessons.explanation: The prefix 小- before a surname or given name makes a friendly, familiar form of address.

examples.chinese: 小王是我的同学。
examples.english: Xiao Wang is my classmate.

lessons.title: 前缀“第-”
lessons.explanation: The prefix 第- before a numeral forms ordinal numbers: 第一 first, 第二 second.

examples.chinese: 今天是我上班的第一天。
examples.english: Today is my first day at work.

examples.chinese: 我是第一个到公司的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì dì-yī gè dào gōngsī de rén.
examples.english: I'm the first person that came to the office.

examples.chinese: 他要坐早上第一班地铁去上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā yào zuò zǎoshang dì-yī bān dìtiě qù shàngbān.
examples.english: He needs to take the first train in the morning to go to work.

allset.title: Ordinal numbers with "di"
allset.note: We use ordinal numbers to express things like "number one" or "second," so mastering them in Chinese is important. Fortunately, they are also very easy to learn by just adding the prefix 第 (dì).

lessons.title: 后缀“-们”
lessons.explanation: The suffix -们 marks plural on pronouns and words for people: 我们, 老师们.

examples.chinese: 我们是学生。
examples.english: We are students.

lessons.title: 后缀“-边”
lessons.explanation: The suffix -边 attaches to direction words to form location words: 上边, 前边, 外边.

examples.chinese: 书在桌子上边。
examples.english: The book is on top of the table.

lessons.title: 方位名词（上、下、里、外、前、后）
lessons.explanation: Locality nouns like 上, 下, 里, 外 follow a noun to express “on / under / inside / outside”.

examples.chinese: 我的书在家里。
examples.english: My book is at home.

lessons.title: 能愿动词“会、能”
lessons.explanation: The modal verbs 会 and 能 before a verb express learned ability (会) or capability/possibility (能).

examples.chinese: 我会说汉语。
examples.english: I can speak Chinese.

lessons.title: 能愿动词“想、要”
lessons.explanation: The modal verbs 想 and 要 before a verb express wanting or intending to do something.

examples.chinese: 我想喝茶。
examples.english: I want to drink tea.

lessons.title: 能愿动词“可以”
lessons.explanation: The modal verb 可以 expresses permission or possibility: “may / be allowed to”.

examples.chinese: 你可以坐这儿。
examples.english: You may sit here.

lessons.title: 离合词（睡觉、说话、上课……）
lessons.explanation: Separable verbs like 睡觉, 说话, 上课 are verb+object compounds that act as one verb, and come apart to take 了 or a measure phrase in the middle.

examples.chinese: 我晚上十点睡觉。
examples.english: I go to bed at ten in the evening.

examples.chinese: 我明天跟他见面 。
examples.english: I'll meet him tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 我不要跟她结婚 。
examples.english: I don't want to marry her.

allset.title: Separable verb
allset.note: "Separable verbs" get their name from their ability to "separate" into two parts (a verb part and an object part), with other words in between. In fact, you could also simply call separable verbs "verb-object phrases."

lessons.title: 人称代词（我、你、您、他、她、大家……）
lessons.explanation: Personal pronouns refer to people; 您 is the polite form of 你.

examples.chinese: 您好，王老师！
examples.english: Hello, Teacher Wang! (polite)

lessons.title: 指示代词（这、那、这儿、那儿、这些……）
lessons.explanation: Demonstratives 这 “this” and 那 “that” point to people, things, and places.

examples.chinese: 这是我的书。
examples.english: This is my book.

lessons.title: 数词（一……十、百、千、半、二/两）
lessons.explanation: Numerals count things; before a measure word, “two” is 两, not 二.

examples.chinese: 我有两个哥哥。
examples.english: I have two older brothers.

lessons.title: 时量词（日、号、岁、点、分、年、天）
lessons.explanation: Time measure words count dates, ages, and clock time; 岁 counts years of age.

examples.chinese: 你儿子几岁？
examples.english: How old is your son?

lessons.title: 程度副词“很、太、非常、真、有点儿”
lessons.explanation: Degree adverbs stand before adjectives; a plain adjective predicate usually takes 很.

examples.chinese: 我今天很忙。
examples.english: I am very busy today.

lessons.title: 范围副词“都”
lessons.explanation: The adverb 都 before the verb means “all / both”, covering everything mentioned before it.

examples.chinese: 我们都是学生。
examples.english: We are all students.

examples.chinese: 你们都认识 John 吗 ？
examples.english: Do you all know John?

examples.chinese: 他们都在上海 。
examples.english: They are all in Shanghai.

allset.title: The "all" adverb "dou"
allset.note: The adverb 都 (dōu) is used to express "all" in Chinese. It's common to use 都 (dōu) in a variety of sentences where it would seem unnecessary in English.

lessons.title: 时间副词“在、正在”
lessons.explanation: 在 or 正在 before the verb marks an action in progress, often with 呢 at the end.

examples.chinese: 他在吃饭。
examples.english: He is eating.

examples.chinese: 她在看书。
examples.english: She is reading.

examples.chinese: 妈妈在打电话。
examples.english: Mom is making a phone call.

allset.title: Expressing actions in progress with "zai"
allset.note: 在 (zài) and 正在 (zhèngzài) can be used as auxiliary verbs to express that an action is ongoing or in progress. This is often the equivalent of present continuous in English, which is how we express that an activity is happening now.

lessons.title: 频率副词“再”
lessons.explanation: The adverb 再 before a verb means “again / once more”, for a repeated future action.

examples.chinese: 你明天再来吧。
examples.english: Come again tomorrow.

lessons.title: 关联副词“也、还”
lessons.explanation: The adverb 也 before the verb means “also / too”, linking a second parallel statement.

examples.chinese: 我是学生，他也是学生。
examples.english: I am a student, and he is a student too.

lessons.title: 介词“在”（引出时间、处所）
lessons.explanation: The preposition 在 introduces the place or time of an action, before the verb.

examples.chinese: 我在学校学习。
examples.english: I study at school.

examples.chinese: 我在上海上大学。
examples.english: I went to college in Shanghai.

examples.chinese: 你一直在这家公司工作吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīzhí zài zhè jiā gōngsī gōngzuò ma?
examples.english: Have you always been working in this company?

allset.title: Indicating location with "zai" before verbs
allset.note: If you need to include the place where an action takes place, you can use 在 (zài). Just pay close attention to word order, as this is one case in which Chinese word order is quite different from English.

lessons.title: 介词“和、对”（引出对象）
lessons.explanation: The preposition 和 introduces the person one does something with; 对 introduces the target “toward”.

examples.chinese: 我和妈妈去商店。
examples.english: I go to the store with Mom.

lessons.title: 连词“和”（连接词语）
lessons.explanation: The conjunction 和 joins nouns or noun phrases: “A and B”.

examples.chinese: 我有一只猫和一只狗。
examples.english: I have a cat and a dog.

lessons.title: 动态助词“了”
lessons.explanation: The aspect particle 了 right after a verb marks a completed action.

examples.chinese: 我买了三本书。
examples.english: I bought three books.

examples.chinese: 他们到了 。
examples.english: They have arrived.

examples.chinese: 我买了 。
examples.english: I've bought it.

allset.title: Expressing completion with "le"
allset.note: The particle 了 (le) has a lot of uses. One of the most common is to express the completion of an action. This is called aspect, which is not the same as tense. Tense is about when an action happens: past, present or future. With regards to 了 (le), aspect is about whether the action is complete in a certain time frame.

lessons.title: 语气助词“呢”
lessons.explanation: Sentence-final 呢 asks “what about…?”, softens a question in progress, or asks where something is.

examples.chinese: 我是老师，你呢？
examples.english: I am a teacher. What about you?

lessons.title: 语气助词“吧”
lessons.explanation: Sentence-final 吧 makes a suggestion or marks an assumption the speaker expects to be right.

examples.chinese: 我们回家吧。
examples.english: Let’s go home.

lessons.title: 语气助词“了”（变化）
lessons.explanation: Sentence-final 了 marks a new situation or change of state: “now / anymore”.

examples.chinese: 天气冷了。
examples.english: The weather has gotten cold.

examples.chinese: 我饿了 。
examples.english: I'm hungry.

examples.chinese: 孩子们都累了 。
examples.english: The kids are all tired.

allset.title: Change of state with "le"
allset.note: 了 (le) has many uses. You probably first learned 了 (le) as a particle that tells you an action is completed, which is also known as "了1." However, this article is not about that use of 了 (le); instead, it is about indicating a change of state (了2). In other words, there is now a new situation, or there is about to be a new situation. This whole "change of state" idea can take numerous forms, and this page includes

lessons.title: 叹词“喂”
lessons.explanation: The interjection 喂 opens a phone call or calls for someone’s attention: “hello?”.

examples.chinese: 喂，你现在忙吗？
examples.english: Hello, are you busy right now?

lessons.title: 主谓句3：名词谓语句
lessons.explanation: A noun phrase serves directly as the predicate for dates, times, ages, and prices: no 是 needed.

examples.chinese: 今天星期一。
examples.english: Today is Monday.

lessons.title: 非主谓句
lessons.explanation: A complete utterance without a subject-predicate structure, common in greetings and requests.

examples.chinese: 请坐，请喝茶。
examples.english: Please sit down and have some tea.

lessons.title: 祈使句（请／不要）
lessons.explanation: Imperatives use 请 for polite requests and 不要 to tell someone not to do something.

examples.chinese: 不要说话。
examples.english: Don’t talk.

lessons.title: 存现句1
lessons.explanation: An existence sentence: a place comes first, then 有 (or 是) introduces what exists there.

examples.chinese: 桌子上有三本书。
examples.english: There are three books on the table.

examples.chinese: 我家有很多小狗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu hěn duō xiǎo gǒu.
examples.english: There are a lot of puppies in my home.

examples.chinese: 我们学校有很多帅哥 。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu hěn duō shuàigē.
examples.english: There are a lot of cute guys in our school.

allset.title: Expressing existence with "you"
allset.note: The verb 有 (yǒu), which means "to have," can also be used to express existence. This is similar to saying "there is" or "there are" in English.

lessons.title: 连动句1
lessons.pattern: 主语＋动词1（＋宾语）＋动词2（＋宾语）
lessons.explanation: Two verbs in sequence share one subject; the first is often 去/来 stating purpose or means.

examples.chinese: 我去商店买苹果。
examples.english: I go to the store to buy apples.

lessons.title: 双宾语句1
lessons.explanation: Some verbs take two objects: first the person, then the thing.

examples.chinese: 妈妈给我十块钱。
examples.english: Mom gives me ten yuan.

lessons.title: 钱数表示法
lessons.explanation: Prices are counted with 块 (colloquial) or 元 (formal): 三块钱 “three yuan”.

examples.chinese: 这个苹果三块钱。
examples.english: This apple is three yuan.

lessons.title: 后缀“-面”
lessons.explanation: The suffix -面 attaches to direction words to form location words: 上面, 里面, 外面.

examples.chinese: 书在桌子上面。
examples.english: The book is on the table.

lessons.title: 方位名词（左、右）
lessons.explanation: The locality nouns 左 “left” and 右 “right” combine with 边/面 to give directions.

examples.chinese: 医院在商店的左边。
examples.english: The hospital is to the left of the store.

lessons.title: 动词重叠
lessons.explanation: Reduplicating a verb (看看, 看一看) makes the action brief, casual, or tentative.

examples.chinese: 我可以看看吗？
examples.english: May I take a look?

lessons.title: 能愿动词“可能”
lessons.explanation: The modal verb 可能 expresses possibility: “might / maybe”.

examples.chinese: 他可能生病了。
examples.english: He might be sick.

lessons.title: 离合词（帮忙、游泳、跳舞、跑步）
lessons.pattern: 游泳 → 游（半个小时的）泳
lessons.explanation: More separable verbs: activity words like 游泳 and 跑步 behave as verb+object compounds, and split when you say how long or how often.

examples.chinese: 我会游泳。
examples.english: I can swim.

lessons.title: 疑问代词“为什么”
lessons.explanation: 为什么 asks for the reason: “why?”.

examples.chinese: 你为什么不吃饭？
examples.english: Why aren’t you eating?

lessons.title: 人称代词“自己”
lessons.explanation: 自己 “oneself” reflects back on the subject or emphasizes doing something personally.

examples.chinese: 这是我自己做的菜。
examples.english: This is a dish I made myself.

lessons.title: 指示代词（这么、那么、这样、那样、每）
lessons.explanation: 这么/那么 before an adjective mean “so / this …”, pointing at degree or manner.

examples.chinese: 今天怎么这么热？
examples.english: Why is it so hot today?

lessons.title: 形容词重叠
lessons.explanation: Reduplicated adjectives (好好, 高高兴兴) intensify and vivify the description.

examples.chinese: 你好好休息吧。
examples.english: Have a good rest.

lessons.title: 数词（万、好多、多）
lessons.explanation: 万 counts ten-thousands; Chinese numbers group by 万, not by thousand.

examples.chinese: 这个电脑一万块钱。
examples.english: This computer costs ten thousand yuan.

lessons.title: 名量词（条、位、间、名；包）
lessons.explanation: More measure words: 条 for long thin things and animals, 位 politely for people, 间 for rooms.

examples.chinese: 我买了一条鱼。
examples.english: I bought a fish.

lessons.title: 动量词“次”
lessons.explanation: The verbal measure word 次 counts how many times an action happens.

examples.chinese: 我去过一次北京。
examples.english: I have been to Beijing once.

lessons.title: 程度副词（多、好、最）
lessons.explanation: The degree adverb 最 marks the superlative: “the most”.

examples.chinese: 我最喜欢吃苹果。
examples.english: I like eating apples the most.

lessons.title: 范围副词“一起”
lessons.explanation: The adverb 一起 before the verb means doing something together.

examples.chinese: 我们一起去吃饭吧。
examples.english: Let’s go eat together.

lessons.title: 时间副词（已经、还、有时候、快、正）
lessons.explanation: Time adverbs like 已经 “already” stand before the verb, often with sentence-final 了.

examples.chinese: 他已经走了。
examples.english: He has already left.

lessons.title: 频率副词“常、经常”
lessons.explanation: The adverb 经常 before the verb means “often / frequently”.

examples.chinese: 我经常去游泳。
examples.english: I often go swimming.

lessons.title: 否定副词“别”
lessons.explanation: 别 before a verb tells someone not to do something: “don’t”.

examples.chinese: 上课别说话。
examples.english: Don’t talk in class.

lessons.title: 关联副词“就”
lessons.explanation: The adverb 就 links two actions in quick sequence: as soon as one happens, the next follows.

examples.chinese: 你到了就给我打电话。
examples.english: Call me as soon as you arrive.

lessons.title: 介词“从”
lessons.explanation: The preposition 从 marks the starting point in time or space: “from”.

examples.chinese: 他从中国来。
examples.english: He comes from China.

lessons.title: 介词“往”
lessons.explanation: The preposition 往 marks the direction of movement: “toward”.

examples.chinese: 请往前走。
examples.english: Please go forward.

lessons.title: 介词“给”
lessons.explanation: The preposition 给 introduces the beneficiary or recipient of an action: “for / to”.

examples.chinese: 我晚上给你打电话。
examples.english: I will call you this evening.

lessons.title: 介词“跟”
lessons.explanation: The preposition 跟 introduces the person one does something with or learns from.

examples.chinese: 明天我跟妈妈去买东西。
examples.english: Tomorrow I am going shopping with Mom.

lessons.title: 连词“那”
lessons.explanation: The conjunction 那 “then / in that case” draws a conclusion from what was just said.

examples.chinese: 你不去，那我自己去。
examples.english: If you are not going, then I will go myself.

lessons.title: 结构助词“得”（状态补语）
lessons.explanation: 得 after a verb links a complement describing how the action is done.

examples.chinese: 他跑得很快。
examples.english: He runs very fast.

lessons.title: 结构助词“地”
lessons.explanation: 地 links an adjective to the verb it modifies, forming an adverbial: 高兴地说.

examples.chinese: 孩子们高兴地唱歌。
examples.english: The children sing happily.

lessons.title: 动态助词“过”
lessons.explanation: The aspect particle 过 after a verb marks past experience: “have (ever) done”.

examples.chinese: 我去过中国。
examples.english: I have been to China.

lessons.title: 动态助词“着”
lessons.explanation: The aspect particle 着 after a verb marks an ongoing state or continuing action.

examples.chinese: 门开着呢。
examples.english: The door is open.

lessons.title: 语气助词“啊”
lessons.explanation: Sentence-final 啊 adds exclamation, agreement, or urging to the sentence.

examples.chinese: 今天天气真好啊！
examples.english: The weather is so nice today!

lessons.title: 固定短语“什么的”
lessons.explanation: 什么的 after a list means “and so on / and such”.

examples.chinese: 我买了苹果、茶什么的。
examples.english: I bought apples, tea, and so on.

lessons.title: 还是……吧
lessons.explanation: 还是……吧 proposes the better alternative after weighing options: “we’d better…”.

examples.chinese: 太晚了，我们还是回家吧。
examples.english: It is too late. We had better go home.

lessons.title: 要/快要/就要……了
lessons.explanation: The frame 要……了 (also 快要/就要……了) marks something about to happen.

examples.chinese: 火车就要开了。
examples.english: The train is about to leave.

lessons.title: 都……了
lessons.explanation: The frame 都……了 stresses that a point has already been reached: “it’s already…”.

examples.chinese: 都十点了，你怎么还在睡觉？
examples.english: It is already ten. Why are you still sleeping?

lessons.title: 结果补语1
lessons.explanation: A result complement right after the verb states the outcome: 完 “finished”, 错 “wrongly”, 懂 “understood”.

examples.chinese: 我吃完饭了。
examples.english: I have finished eating.

lessons.title: 趋向补语1
lessons.explanation: Directional complements 来/去 (and 进来, 回来…) after a verb show movement toward or away from the speaker.

examples.chinese: 你快进来吧。
examples.english: Come on in.

lessons.title: 数量补语2（时量）
lessons.explanation: A duration complement after the verb states how long the action lasts.

examples.chinese: 我睡了八个小时。
examples.english: I slept for eight hours.

lessons.title: 主谓句4：主谓谓语句
lessons.explanation: A subject-predicate phrase itself serves as the predicate: 我身体很好 “my health is good”.

examples.chinese: 我身体很好。
examples.english: My health is very good.

lessons.title: 选择问句“还是”
lessons.explanation: 还是 joins two alternatives in a choice question: “A or B?”, also inside a sentence after 不知道 or 不管.

examples.chinese: 你喝茶还是喝咖啡？
examples.english: Do you want tea or coffee?

lessons.title: “是”字句2（说明或特征）
lessons.explanation: 是 links the subject to a description or characteristic, often with a 的-phrase.

examples.chinese: 这件衣服是红的。
examples.english: This piece of clothing is red.

lessons.title: “有”字句2（达到）
lessons.explanation: 有 before a quantity or comparison states that an amount or degree is reached.

examples.chinese: 从我家到学校有二十分钟。
examples.english: It takes a good twenty minutes from my home to school.

lessons.title: 存现句2
lessons.pattern: 处所＋动词＋着（＋数量短语）＋名词
lessons.explanation: An existence sentence with verb+着: a place comes first, then what is there in that state.

examples.chinese: 椅子上坐着一个人。
examples.english: A person is sitting on the chair.

lessons.title: 比较句1
lessons.explanation: 比 compares two things: A is more … than B; a measure of difference can follow.

examples.chinese: 他比我高。
examples.english: He is taller than me.

lessons.title: “是……的”句1
lessons.pattern: 是＋时间/地点/方式＋动词＋的
lessons.explanation: The 是……的 frame highlights the time, place, manner, or agent of a past action.

examples.chinese: 你是什么时候来的？
examples.english: When was it that you came?

lessons.title: 兼语句1
lessons.pattern: 主语＋请/叫/让＋宾语1＋动词（＋宾语2）
lessons.explanation: A pivotal sentence: the object of 请/叫/让 is also the subject of the following verb.

examples.chinese: 我想请你吃饭。
examples.english: I would like to invite you to a meal.

lessons.title: 双宾语句2
lessons.explanation: Verbs like 送 and 带 combine with 给 before the recipient and the thing given.

examples.chinese: 他送给我一本书。
examples.english: He gave me a book as a gift.

lessons.title: 紧缩复句“一……就……”
lessons.explanation: The frame 一…就… means “as soon as A happens, B happens”.

examples.chinese: 我一到家就给你打电话。
examples.english: I will call you as soon as I get home.

lessons.title: 转折复句“虽然……但是……”
lessons.explanation: 虽然…但是… links two clauses with a contrast: “although… , but…”.

examples.chinese: 虽然很贵，但是我很喜欢。
examples.english: Although it is expensive, I like it very much.

lessons.title: 因果复句“因为……所以……”
lessons.explanation: 因为…所以… links cause and result: “because… , therefore…”.

examples.chinese: 因为下雨，所以我没去跑步。
examples.english: Because it rained, I did not go running.

lessons.title: 概数表达法1
lessons.explanation: Approximate numbers use 几 or add 多 after the numeral: 十多个 “ten-odd”.

examples.chinese: 我买了十多个苹果。
examples.english: I bought more than ten apples.

lessons.title: 前缀“老-”
lessons.explanation: Prefix 老- before a surname forms a familiar way to address someone.

examples.chinese: 老王是我爸爸的老朋友。
examples.english: Lao Wang is an old friend of my father.

lessons.title: 后缀“-员／-家／-子”
lessons.explanation: Suffixes like -员 form nouns for people with a role or job.

examples.chinese: 她是饭店的服务员。
examples.english: She is a waitress at the restaurant.

lessons.title: 能愿动词“应该”
lessons.explanation: 应该 expresses what should or ought to be done.

examples.chinese: 你应该早点儿睡觉。
examples.english: You should go to bed earlier.

lessons.title: 离合词
lessons.explanation: Separable verbs like 洗澡 can split to take 了, 个 or other material in the middle.

examples.chinese: 他每天晚上都洗澡。
examples.english: He takes a shower every evening.

lessons.title: 疑问代词的任指用法
lessons.explanation: Question words + 都/也 mean “any / every”: 什么都, 谁都.

examples.chinese: 他什么都想学。
examples.english: He wants to learn everything.

lessons.title: 人称代词“咱们”
lessons.explanation: 咱们 means “we”, always including the listener.

examples.chinese: 咱们一起去吃饭吧。
examples.english: Let us go eat together.

lessons.title: 指示代词“别的／其他”
lessons.explanation: 别的 means “other / something else”.

examples.chinese: 我不要别的，就要这个。
examples.english: I do not want anything else, just this one.

lessons.title: 量词重叠与数量重叠
lessons.explanation: Reduplicated measure words mean “every one”; 一M一M means “one by one”.

examples.chinese: 他们个个都很高兴。
examples.english: Every one of them is very happy.

lessons.title: 动量词“遍”
lessons.explanation: Verbal measure word 遍 counts complete run-throughs of an action.

examples.chinese: 请你再说一遍。
examples.english: Please say it one more time.

lessons.title: 程度副词“更”
lessons.explanation: 更 means “even more”, raising the degree in a comparison.

examples.chinese: 今天比昨天更冷。
examples.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

lessons.title: 范围副词“一共”
lessons.explanation: 一共 means “altogether, in total”.

examples.chinese: 我们班一共有二十人。
examples.english: Our class has twenty people in total.

lessons.title: 时间副词“才”
lessons.explanation: 才 marks that something happens later than expected: “not until”.

examples.chinese: 他十点才起床。
examples.english: He did not get up until ten o'clock.

lessons.title: 频率副词“总是”
lessons.explanation: 总是 means “always”.

examples.chinese: 他总是第一个到学校。
examples.english: He is always the first to arrive at school.

lessons.title: 情态副词“一定”
lessons.explanation: 一定 means “definitely, must”.

examples.chinese: 明天我一定来。
examples.english: I will definitely come tomorrow.

lessons.title: 语气副词“终于”
lessons.explanation: 终于 means “finally, at last” after a long wait or effort.

examples.chinese: 我们终于到北京了。
examples.english: We finally arrived in Beijing.

lessons.title: 否定副词“不用／不必”
lessons.explanation: 不用 means “no need to”.

examples.chinese: 你不用担心我。
examples.english: You do not need to worry about me.

lessons.title: 介词“关于”
lessons.explanation: 关于 introduces the topic “about, concerning”.

examples.chinese: 这是一本关于中国的书。
examples.english: This is a book about China.

lessons.title: 介词“根据”
lessons.explanation: 根据 means “according to, based on”.

examples.chinese: 请根据要求写句子。
examples.english: Please write sentences according to the requirements.

lessons.title: 介词“为了”与目的复句
lessons.explanation: 为了 introduces the purpose “in order to, for the sake of”.

examples.chinese: 为了健康，他每天跑步。
examples.english: For his health, he runs every day.

lessons.title: 连词“或者”与选择复句
lessons.explanation: 或者 offers alternatives in statements and suggestions: “or / either… or…”. A question “A or B?” takes 还是.

examples.chinese: 我们坐公交车或者地铁去。
examples.english: We'll go by bus or subway.

lessons.title: 助词“的话”
lessons.explanation: 的话 after a clause marks “if…”, often paired with 就.

examples.chinese: 你有时间的话，就来我家玩。
examples.english: If you have time, come to my place.

lessons.title: 四字格“不A不B”
lessons.explanation: 不A不B with opposite words means “neither too A nor too B, just right”.

examples.chinese: 这件衣服不大不小。
examples.english: This piece of clothing is neither too big nor too small.

lessons.title: 越来越……
lessons.explanation: 越来越 means “more and more” over time.

examples.chinese: 天气越来越热了。
examples.english: The weather is getting hotter and hotter.

lessons.title: 看起来／看上去／在……看来
lessons.explanation: 看起来 means “it seems / looks like”; 在……看来 gives a point of view.

examples.chinese: 你今天看起来很累。
examples.english: You look very tired today.

lessons.title: 对……来说／一般来说
lessons.explanation: 对……来说 means “as far as… is concerned”; 一般来说 means “generally speaking”.

examples.chinese: 对我来说，汉字最难。
examples.english: For me, Chinese characters are the hardest.

lessons.title: 除了……（以外），还／也／都……
lessons.explanation: 除了 means “besides / except”, often with 还, 也 or 都.

examples.chinese: 除了汉语，他还会英语。
examples.english: Besides Chinese, he also speaks English.

lessons.title: 从……起
lessons.explanation: 从……起 means “starting from (a time)”.

examples.chinese: 从明天起，我要早点儿起床。
examples.english: Starting tomorrow, I will get up earlier.

lessons.title: 一……也／都＋不／没……
lessons.explanation: 一…也/都 + negation means “not even one / not at all”.

examples.chinese: 他一句话也没说。
examples.english: He did not say a single word.

lessons.title: 越……越……
lessons.explanation: 越…越… means “the more…, the more…”.

examples.chinese: 雨越下越大了。
examples.english: The rain is falling harder and harder.

lessons.title: （在）……以前／以后
lessons.explanation: 以前/以后 after a phrase mean “before / after …”.

examples.chinese: 下课以后我们去打球。
examples.english: After class we will go play ball.

lessons.title: 该……了
lessons.explanation: 该…了 means “it is time to…”.

examples.chinese: 十点了，该睡觉了。
examples.english: It is ten o'clock; time to sleep.

lessons.title: 在……上／下／中
lessons.explanation: 在…下 frames a condition, e.g. “with the help of…”.

examples.chinese: 在老师的帮助下，成绩提高了。
examples.english: With the teacher's help, my grades improved.

lessons.title: X什么（啊）
lessons.explanation: Verb + 什么（啊） dismisses an action: “what are you …-ing for?”.

examples.chinese: 哭什么啊，没事了。
examples.english: What are you crying for? It is all right now.

lessons.title: 结果补语“到／住／走／上”
lessons.explanation: Result complements like 到 mark that the action reached its result.

examples.chinese: 我找到手机了。
examples.english: I found my phone.

lessons.title: 趋向补语的引申用法
lessons.explanation: Directional complements extend to meanings like starting (起来) or continuing (下去).

examples.chinese: 大家都笑了起来。
examples.english: Everyone started laughing.

lessons.title: 可能补语1
lessons.explanation: V + 得/不 + complement says whether a result can be achieved.

examples.chinese: 黑板上的字你看得清楚吗？
examples.english: Can you see the characters on the blackboard clearly?

lessons.title: 程度补语“极了／得很”
lessons.explanation: 极了 after an adjective means “extremely”.

examples.chinese: 今天天气热极了。
examples.english: The weather today is extremely hot.

lessons.title: 数量补语（时间间隔）
lessons.explanation: A duration after the verb + 了 marks time elapsed since an event.

examples.chinese: 他离开北京三年了。
examples.english: It has been three years since he left Beijing.

lessons.title: “怎样＋动词”的特指问句
lessons.explanation: 怎样 + verb asks “how” something is done.

examples.chinese: 这个字怎样读？
examples.english: How is this character read?

lessons.title: 反问句“不是……吗？”
lessons.explanation: Rhetorical 不是…吗 emphasizes something the listener should know.

examples.chinese: 你不是去过北京吗？
examples.english: Have you not been to Beijing before?

lessons.title: “把”字句1
lessons.pattern: 主语＋把＋宾语＋动词＋其他成分
lessons.explanation: The 把 sentence moves the object before the verb to show what is done to it.

examples.chinese: 请你把门关上。
examples.english: Please close the door.

lessons.title: 被动句1
lessons.pattern: 主语＋被（＋宾语）＋动词＋其他成分
lessons.explanation: The 被 sentence marks the subject as affected by an action.

examples.chinese: 我的蛋糕被弟弟吃了。
examples.english: My cake was eaten by my younger brother.

lessons.title: 连动句“着”
lessons.explanation: V1着V2 shows the first action accompanying the second.

examples.chinese: 他笑着回答问题。
examples.english: He answered the question with a smile.

lessons.title: 比较句2
lessons.explanation: 比 compares two things, with 更/还, 不比, or a measured difference.

examples.chinese: 他比我更喜欢运动。
examples.english: He likes sports even more than I do.

lessons.title: 跟……一样
lessons.explanation: 跟…一样 says two things are the same (optionally in some quality).

examples.chinese: 我的书包跟你的一样。
examples.english: My schoolbag is the same as yours.

lessons.title: 存现句3
lessons.pattern: 处所词＋动词＋补语＋了＋数量＋人／物
lessons.explanation: Existential sentences report someone or something appearing or disappearing at a place.

examples.chinese: 我们班来了一个新同学。
examples.english: A new classmate came to our class.

lessons.title: “是……的”句2
lessons.explanation: 是…的 here emphasizes the speaker's view or attitude.

examples.chinese: 放心吧，他是会来的。
examples.english: Do not worry; he will definitely come.

lessons.title: 重动句
lessons.pattern: 主语＋动词＋宾语＋动词＋补语
lessons.explanation: The verb is repeated after its object so a complement can follow.

examples.chinese: 他说汉语说得很好。
examples.english: He speaks Chinese very well.

lessons.title: 承接复句
lessons.explanation: 先…然后/再… orders actions in sequence.

examples.chinese: 我们先吃饭，然后看电影。
examples.english: We will eat first and then watch a movie.

lessons.title: 并列复句“一会儿……，一会儿……”
lessons.explanation: 一会儿…一会儿… marks quick alternation between actions or states.

examples.chinese: 天气一会儿冷，一会儿热。
examples.english: The weather is cold one moment and hot the next.

lessons.title: 并列复句“又……，又……”
lessons.explanation: 又…又… joins two qualities or actions that hold at once.

examples.chinese: 这个西瓜又大又甜。
examples.english: This watermelon is both big and sweet.

lessons.title: 并列复句“一边……，一边……”
lessons.explanation: 一边…一边… marks two actions done at the same time.

examples.chinese: 他一边走路，一边听音乐。
examples.english: He listens to music while walking.

lessons.title: 递进复句
lessons.explanation: 不但…而且… means “not only… but also…”.

examples.chinese: 他不但会开车，而且开得很好。
examples.english: He can not only drive but drives very well.

lessons.title: 转折复句
lessons.explanation: 虽然…可是… means “although…, but…”.

examples.chinese: 虽然下雨了，可是他还是来了。
examples.english: Although it rained, he still came.

lessons.title: 假设复句
lessons.explanation: 如果…就… means “if…, then…”.

examples.chinese: 如果明天不下雨，我们就去爬山。
examples.english: If it does not rain tomorrow, we will go hiking.

lessons.title: 条件复句“只有……，才……”
lessons.explanation: 只有…才… states a necessary condition: “only if…”.

examples.chinese: 只有多练习，才能学好汉语。
examples.english: Only by practicing a lot can you learn Chinese well.

lessons.title: 条件复句“只要……，就……”
lessons.explanation: 只要…就… states a sufficient condition: “as long as…”.

examples.chinese: 只要努力，成绩就会提高。
examples.english: As long as you work hard, your grades will improve.

lessons.title: 紧缩复句
lessons.explanation: Compressed clauses: as soon as one action finishes, the next follows with 就.

examples.chinese: 他下了课就回家。
examples.english: He goes home as soon as class is over.

lessons.title: 概数表达法2
lessons.pattern: 大概＋数量／相邻数词连用
lessons.explanation: 大概 or two adjacent numbers express an approximate amount.

examples.chinese: 教室里大概有三十个人。
examples.english: There are about thirty people in the classroom.

lessons.title: 能愿动词“敢”
lessons.explanation: 敢 means “to dare to”.

examples.chinese: 我不敢告诉妈妈这件事。
examples.english: I dare not tell Mom about this.

lessons.title: 指示代词“任何／各／此”
lessons.explanation: 任何 means “any”, usually reinforced with 都.

examples.chinese: 任何人都可以参加。
examples.english: Anyone can take part.

lessons.title: 动量词“趟／场／顿”
lessons.explanation: Verbal measure words like 趟 count trips or rounds of an action.

examples.chinese: 我去了一趟银行。
examples.english: I made a trip to the bank.

lessons.title: 程度副词“十分”
lessons.explanation: 十分 means “very, fully” (a formal “extremely”).

examples.chinese: 他对这次考试十分满意。
examples.english: He is very satisfied with this exam.

lessons.title: 范围副词“至少”
lessons.explanation: 至少 means “at least”.

examples.chinese: 从这儿到机场至少要一个小时。
examples.english: It takes at least an hour from here to the airport.

lessons.title: 时间副词“从来”
lessons.explanation: 从来 with negation means “never (up to now)”.

examples.chinese: 他从来不迟到。
examples.english: He is never late.

lessons.title: 频率副词“重新”
lessons.explanation: 重新 means “anew, all over again”.

examples.chinese: 这篇文章我要重新写一遍。
examples.english: I will rewrite this article from scratch.

lessons.title: 方式副词“互相”
lessons.explanation: 互相 means “mutually, each other”.

examples.chinese: 同学们应该互相帮助。
examples.english: Classmates should help each other.

lessons.title: 关联副词“却”
lessons.explanation: 却 marks an unexpected contrast: “yet, however”.

examples.chinese: 他答应来，却没有来。
examples.english: He promised to come, yet he did not.

lessons.title: 情态副词“恐怕／也许”
lessons.explanation: 恐怕 means “I am afraid that…”, marking a worried guess.

examples.chinese: 恐怕明天要下雨。
examples.english: I am afraid it will rain tomorrow.

lessons.title: 语气副词“竟然”
lessons.explanation: 竟然 marks surprise: “unexpectedly, to my surprise”.

examples.chinese: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
examples.english: He actually forgot his own birthday.

lessons.title: 介词“随着”
lessons.explanation: 随着 means “along with, as (something changes)”.

examples.chinese: 随着时间过去，他习惯了这里的生活。
examples.english: As time passed, he got used to life here.

lessons.title: 介词“由”
lessons.explanation: 由 introduces the agent responsible: “to be done by…”.

examples.chinese: 这件事由我来负责。
examples.english: I will be responsible for this matter.

lessons.title: 介词“对于”
lessons.explanation: 对于 introduces the object of an attitude or comment: “regarding”.

examples.chinese: 对于这个问题，大家的看法不同。
examples.english: Regarding this question, people have different views.

lessons.title: 介词“按照／按”
lessons.explanation: 按照 means “according to, in line with”.

examples.chinese: 请按照老师说的做。
examples.english: Please do as the teacher says.

lessons.title: 连词“并（且）”
lessons.explanation: 并且/并 joins verbs or clauses: “and, moreover”.

examples.chinese: 我同意这个办法，并且愿意帮忙。
examples.english: I agree with this plan and am willing to help.

lessons.title: 助词“等”
lessons.explanation: 等 after a list means “and so on, etc.”.

examples.chinese: 桌子上放着苹果、香蕉等水果。
examples.english: On the table are apples, bananas and other fruit.

lessons.title: 数词＋形容词＋量词
lessons.explanation: An adjective can slot between number and measure word: 一大杯, 一大袋.

examples.chinese: 他买了一大袋水果。
examples.english: He bought a big bag of fruit.

lessons.title: 四字格“一A一B／有A有B／无A无B”
lessons.explanation: Four-character frames like 有说有笑 pack two parallel actions or qualities.

examples.chinese: 孩子们有说有笑地走进教室。
examples.english: The children walked into the classroom talking and laughing.

lessons.title: 来得及／来不及
lessons.explanation: 来得及/来不及 say whether there is still time to do something.

examples.chinese: 再不出发就来不及了。
examples.english: If we do not leave now, there will be no time.

lessons.title: 有的是
lessons.explanation: 有的是 means “to have plenty of”.

examples.chinese: 别着急，我们有的是时间。
examples.english: Do not worry; we have plenty of time.

lessons.title: 说不定
lessons.explanation: 说不定 means “perhaps, you never know”.

examples.chinese: 你问问他，说不定他知道。
examples.english: Ask him; he might just know.

lessons.title: 就是说／这就是说
lessons.explanation: 就是说 restates something: “that is to say”.

examples.chinese: 他没回短信，就是说他可能很忙。
examples.english: He did not reply, which means he is probably busy.

lessons.title: 一＋量词＋比＋一＋量词
lessons.explanation: One-M-比-one-M shows steady change: 一天比一天 “day by day”.

examples.chinese: 天气一天比一天热。
examples.english: The weather is getting hotter day by day.

lessons.title: 在……方面
lessons.explanation: 在…方面 means “in the area of, as regards”.

examples.chinese: 在学习方面，他从来不让人担心。
examples.english: When it comes to studying, he never worries anyone.

lessons.title: 够……的
lessons.explanation: 够…的 emphasizes a high degree: “really quite…”.

examples.chinese: 今天可真够热的。
examples.english: It is really quite hot today.

lessons.title: 拿……来说
lessons.explanation: 拿…来说 means “take… for example”.

examples.chinese: 拿我们班来说，一半人会游泳。
examples.english: Take our class: half the people can swim.

lessons.title: 再也不／没……
lessons.explanation: 再也 + negation means “never again”.

examples.chinese: 我再也不想看这部电影了。
examples.english: I never want to watch this movie again.

lessons.title: 怎么都／也＋不／没……
lessons.explanation: 怎么都/也 + negation means “no matter how, just cannot”.

examples.chinese: 这个门怎么都打不开。
examples.english: This door just will not open no matter what.

lessons.title: 为了……而……
lessons.explanation: 为了 A 而 B: do B for the sake of A.

examples.chinese: 他为了考上大学而努力学习。
examples.english: He studies hard in order to get into university.

lessons.title: X是X（一X是一X／X是X，Y是Y）
lessons.explanation: 是-frames concede or separate: 能V一点是一点; A是A，B是B.

examples.chinese: 时间不多了，能多学一点是一点。
examples.english: Time is short; every bit more we learn counts.

lessons.title: X也得X，不X也得X／说什么也得X
lessons.explanation: 也得-frames insist there is no way around doing something.

examples.chinese: 这件事你去也得去，不去也得去。
examples.english: You must go whether you want to or not.

lessons.title: （没）有什么（好）X的
lessons.explanation: 没什么好X的 means “there is nothing worth X-ing about”.

examples.chinese: 这件事没有什么好担心的。
examples.english: There is nothing to worry about in this matter.

lessons.title: X就X（点儿）吧／X就是了
lessons.explanation: 就-frames accept something or reassure: “fine, so be it / just do it”.

examples.chinese: 贵就贵点儿吧，东西好就行。
examples.english: If it is expensive, so be it, as long as it is good.

lessons.title: 还X呢
lessons.explanation: 还X呢 mocks a mismatch between a label and reality.

examples.chinese: 还大学生呢，这个字都不认识。
examples.english: Some university student you are; you do not even know this character.

lessons.title: 你X你的（吧）
lessons.explanation: 你X你的 tells someone to carry on with their own business.

examples.chinese: 你忙你的吧，我自己来。
examples.english: You go on with your work; I will manage myself.

lessons.title: 程度补语2
lessons.pattern: 形容词／心理动词＋死了／得厉害
lessons.explanation: 死了 after adjectives or feeling verbs means “to death, terribly”.

examples.chinese: 走了一天，我累死了。
examples.english: After walking all day, I am dead tired.

lessons.title: 可能补语2
lessons.explanation: V得了/V不了 say whether an action is possible or manageable.

examples.chinese: 这么多菜，我一个人吃不了。
examples.english: So much food; I cannot eat it all by myself.

lessons.title: 反问句2
lessons.explanation: 难道…吗 forms a rhetorical question expressing disbelief.

examples.chinese: 难道你忘了吗？
examples.english: Do not tell me you forgot?

lessons.title: “把”字句2
lessons.pattern: 主语＋把＋宾语＋动词＋了／一下／动量补语
lessons.explanation: Extended 把 patterns with 了, reduplication, or measure complements.

examples.chinese: 你把这句话再读一遍。
examples.english: Read this sentence once more.

lessons.title: 被动句2
lessons.pattern: 主语＋叫／让＋宾语＋动词＋其他成分
lessons.explanation: 叫/让 mark colloquial passives like 被.

examples.chinese: 蛋糕让弟弟吃完了。
examples.english: The cake was finished off by my little brother.

lessons.title: 兼语句2
lessons.explanation: Pivotal sentences with 使/让 express causing someone to feel or do something.

examples.chinese: 这个消息使大家很高兴。
examples.english: This news made everyone very happy.

lessons.title: 比较句3“A不如B”
lessons.explanation: 不如 means “not as good as / not as … as”.

examples.chinese: 我的汉语不如他好。
examples.english: My Chinese is not as good as his.

lessons.title: 跟……相比
lessons.explanation: 跟…相比 sets up a comparison: “compared with…”.

examples.chinese: 跟去年相比，今年冬天冷多了。
examples.english: Compared with last year, this winter is much colder.

lessons.title: 双重否定句
lessons.explanation: Double negation emphasizes a strong affirmative.

examples.chinese: 班里没有人不认识他。
examples.english: There is no one in the class who does not know him.

lessons.title: 并列复句“不是……，而是……”
lessons.explanation: 不是A而是B corrects: “not A but B”.

examples.chinese: 他不是不想去，而是没有时间。
examples.english: It is not that he does not want to go, but that he has no time.

lessons.title: 并列复句“既……，又／也……”
lessons.explanation: 既A又B joins two coexisting qualities or actions.

examples.chinese: 这个房间既干净又安静。
examples.english: This room is both clean and quiet.

lessons.title: 并列复句“一方面……，另一方面……”
lessons.explanation: 一方面…另一方面… presents two sides of a matter.

examples.chinese: 他一方面想去，另一方面又怕花钱。
examples.english: On one hand he wants to go; on the other he fears spending money.

lessons.title: 承接复句“首先……，其次／然后……”
lessons.explanation: 首先…其次/然后… lists steps or points in order.

examples.chinese: 首先要努力，其次要有好方法。
examples.english: First you must work hard; second you need good methods.

lessons.title: 承接复句“……，于是……”
lessons.explanation: 于是 links a situation to what happened as a result: “and so”.

examples.chinese: 外面下雨了，于是我们留在家里。
examples.english: It started raining outside, so we stayed home.

lessons.title: 递进复句“……，甚至……”
lessons.explanation: 甚至 pushes to an extreme case: “even”.

examples.chinese: 他忙得甚至忘了吃饭。
examples.english: He was so busy he even forgot to eat.

lessons.title: 递进复句“不仅／不光……，还／而且……”
lessons.explanation: 不仅…还… means “not only… but also…”.

examples.chinese: 她不仅会英语，还会汉语。
examples.english: She knows not only English but also Chinese.

lessons.title: 递进复句“连……也／都……”
lessons.explanation: 连…也/都 highlights an extreme case: “even”.

examples.chinese: 他忙得连饭都没吃。
examples.english: He was so busy he did not even eat.

lessons.title: 选择复句“不是……，就是……”
lessons.explanation: 不是A就是B means “if not A, then B, always one of the two”.

examples.chinese: 他周末不是打球，就是游泳。
examples.english: On weekends he is either playing ball or swimming.

lessons.title: 转折复句“尽管……，但是／可是……”
lessons.explanation: 尽管 concedes a fact before the contrast: “even though”.

examples.chinese: 尽管很难，但是他没有放弃。
examples.english: Even though it was hard, he did not give up.

lessons.title: 转折复句“……，然而……”
lessons.explanation: 然而 is a formal “however”.

examples.chinese: 他试了很多次，然而都失败了。
examples.english: He tried many times; however, he failed every time.

lessons.title: 转折复句“……，不过……”
lessons.explanation: 不过 adds a mild reservation: “but, though”.

examples.chinese: 这个手机不错，不过有点儿贵。
examples.english: This phone is good, though a bit expensive.

lessons.title: 假设复句“……，否则……”
lessons.explanation: 否则 warns of the alternative: “otherwise”.

examples.chinese: 快点儿走，否则要迟到了。
examples.english: Hurry up, otherwise we will be late.

lessons.title: 假设复句“要是……，就……”
lessons.explanation: 要是…就… is a colloquial “if…, then…”.

examples.chinese: 要是明天天气好，我们就去公园。
examples.english: If the weather is good tomorrow, we will go to the park.

lessons.title: 条件复句“不管／无论……，都／也……”
lessons.explanation: 不管/无论…都… means “no matter…, still…”.

examples.chinese: 不管天气怎么样，我们都去。
examples.english: No matter what the weather is like, we will go.

lessons.title: 因果复句“既然……，就……”
lessons.explanation: 既然…就… draws a conclusion from a given fact: “since…”.

examples.chinese: 既然你不舒服，就在家休息吧。
examples.english: Since you are not feeling well, rest at home.

lessons.title: 因果复句“（由于）……，因此……”
lessons.explanation: 因此 states the consequence: “therefore”.

examples.chinese: 他平时很努力，因此成绩很好。
examples.english: He usually works hard; therefore his grades are good.

lessons.title: 目的复句“……，好……”
lessons.explanation: 好 introduces the intended purpose: “so that…”.

examples.chinese: 请把地址写清楚，好让司机找到你。
examples.english: Write the address clearly so the driver can find you.

lessons.title: 让步复句“即使／就是……，也……”
lessons.explanation: 即使/就是…也… concedes a hypothetical: “even if…”.

examples.chinese: 即使下雨，我们也要去。
examples.english: Even if it rains, we will still go.

lessons.title: 紧缩复句“不……也……”
lessons.explanation: Compressed “even without A, B still holds”.

examples.chinese: 你不说我也知道。
examples.english: Even if you do not say it, I still know.

lessons.title: 概数表示法3
lessons.pattern: 数词＋来＋量词／大约／左右／前后
lessons.explanation: 左右 after an amount, or 数+来+量, expresses “approximately”.

examples.chinese: 现在是下午五点左右。
examples.english: It is around five in the afternoon now.

lessons.title: 倍数、分数、百分数的表示法
lessons.explanation: 倍 expresses multiples: A是B的两倍, 多了一倍.

examples.chinese: 今年的学生是去年的两倍。
examples.english: This year's students are double last year's.

lessons.title: 后缀“-头”
lessons.explanation: Noun suffix -头 forming everyday nouns (石头, 木头, 念头).

examples.chinese: 他捡起一块石头扔进了河里。
examples.english: He picked up a stone and threw it into the river.

lessons.title: 指示代词“彼此、如此、本”
lessons.explanation: Demonstrative pronouns: 彼此 (each other), 如此 (so/like this), 本 (this/one’s own).

examples.chinese: 老朋友之间应该彼此信任。
examples.english: Old friends should trust each other.

lessons.title: 名量词“册、朵、届、颗、匹、行、架、群、支、根、批、束、副、集、周”
lessons.explanation: Level-5 nominal measure words such as 颗 for small round things.

examples.chinese: 天上有几颗星星特别亮。
examples.english: A few stars in the sky are especially bright.

lessons.title: 动量词“眼”
lessons.explanation: Verbal measure word 眼: a glance (看一眼).

examples.chinese: 他回头看了我一眼，什么也没说。
examples.english: He turned and gave me a glance without saying anything.

lessons.title: 程度副词“过于、相当、较、可、格外、极其”
lessons.explanation: Degree adverbs; 格外 = especially, exceptionally.

examples.chinese: 下过雨后，空气格外新鲜。
examples.english: After the rain, the air is especially fresh.

lessons.title: 时间副词“时刻、曾经、立刻、连忙、始终、早已、即将、急忙、渐渐、尽快、早晚”
lessons.explanation: Time adverbs; 曾经 marks a past experience: once, at some time.

examples.chinese: 我曾经在上海住过三年。
examples.english: I once lived in Shanghai for three years.

lessons.title: 频率副词“老是、通常、时常”
lessons.explanation: Frequency adverbs; 老是 = always, again and again (often complaining).

examples.chinese: 他上课老是迟到，老师很生气。
examples.english: He is always late for class, and the teacher is angry.

lessons.title: 方式副词“尽量、亲自”
lessons.explanation: Manner adverbs; 亲自 = in person, personally.

examples.chinese: 这件事经理要亲自处理。
examples.english: The manager wants to handle this matter personally.

lessons.title: 关联副词“便、一旦”
lessons.explanation: Linking adverbs; 便 = then, thereupon (written equivalent of 就).

examples.chinese: 他说完便转身离开了。
examples.english: As soon as he finished speaking, he turned and left.

lessons.title: 情态副词“似乎、仿佛”
lessons.explanation: Modal adverbs; 似乎 = it seems, apparently.

examples.chinese: 他似乎不太愿意谈这件事。
examples.english: He seems unwilling to talk about this matter.

lessons.title: 语气副词“毕竟、居然、反正、根本、果然、简直、绝对、的确、反而、白、刚好、可”
lessons.explanation: Tone adverbs; 居然 = unexpectedly, to one’s surprise.

examples.chinese: 他居然忘了自己的生日。
examples.english: He actually forgot his own birthday.

lessons.title: 介词“自从”（引出时间、处所）
lessons.explanation: Preposition 自从: ever since (a past starting point).

examples.chinese: 自从搬到北京，我们很少见面了。
examples.english: Since moving to Beijing, we rarely see each other.

lessons.title: 介词“朝、沿（着）”（引出方向、路径）
lessons.explanation: Prepositions of direction/path; 朝 = toward.

examples.chinese: 他朝我挥了挥手。
examples.english: He waved his hand at me.

lessons.title: 介词“替、同、较”（引出对象）
lessons.explanation: Object-introducing prepositions; 替 = for, on behalf of.

examples.chinese: 你放心去吧，我替你照顾小狗。
examples.english: Go without worry; I will look after the puppy for you.

lessons.title: 介词“凭、据、依据”（引出凭借、依据）
lessons.explanation: Prepositions of basis; 凭 = on the basis of, by virtue of.

examples.chinese: 凭这张票可以免费进入公园。
examples.english: With this ticket you can enter the park for free.

lessons.title: 连词“以及、同”（连接词或词组）
lessons.explanation: Conjunctions joining words/phrases; 以及 = as well as.

examples.chinese: 会议讨论了价格、质量以及服务问题。
examples.english: The meeting discussed price, quality, as well as service issues.

lessons.title: 连词“从而、可见、假如、总之”（连接分句或句子）
lessons.explanation: Clause-linking conjunctions; 总之 = in short, anyway.

examples.chinese: 总之，这次活动办得很成功。
examples.english: In short, this event was a great success.

lessons.title: 助词“似的”
lessons.explanation: Particle 似的 after a noun/phrase: like, as if.

examples.chinese: 他高兴得像个孩子似的。
examples.english: He is as happy as a child.

lessons.title: 四字格“A来A去”
lessons.explanation: V来V去: doing the action back and forth, over and over.

examples.chinese: 我想来想去，还是决定留下来。
examples.english: After thinking it over and over, I decided to stay after all.

lessons.title: 四字格“A着A着”
lessons.explanation: V着V着: while doing something, another change happens.

examples.chinese: 她说着说着就哭了。
examples.english: As she was talking, she started to cry.

lessons.title: 四字格“没A没B”
lessons.explanation: 没A没B: emphatic negation, e.g. 没完没了 = endless.

examples.chinese: 他一说起足球就没完没了。
examples.english: Once he starts talking about football, he goes on endlessly.

lessons.title: 四字格“说A就A”
lessons.explanation: 说A就A: doing something right away, without hesitation.

examples.chinese: 他说走就走，谁也拦不住。
examples.english: When he says he is leaving, he leaves at once; no one can stop him.

lessons.title: 固定短语“不得了”
lessons.explanation: 不得了: terrible / extraordinary; also exclamation of alarm.

examples.chinese: 不得了了，火车马上就要开了！
examples.english: Oh no, the train is about to leave!

lessons.title: 固定短语“用不着”
lessons.explanation: 用不着: there is no need to.

examples.chinese: 这点小事，用不着麻烦别人。
examples.english: For such a small matter, there is no need to trouble others.

lessons.title: 从……来看
lessons.explanation: Judging from …, from the perspective of ….

examples.chinese: 从结果来看，我们的方法是对的。
examples.english: Judging from the result, our method was right.

lessons.title: A的A，B的B
lessons.explanation: Some doing A, others doing B. Everyone busy in their own way.

examples.chinese: 晚会上，大家唱歌的唱歌，跳舞的跳舞。
examples.english: At the party, some were singing and some were dancing.

lessons.title: （自）……以来
lessons.explanation: Since … (up to now).

examples.chinese: 自开学以来，他一次课都没缺过。
examples.english: Since the semester started, he has not missed a single class.

lessons.title: 由……组成
lessons.explanation: To be made up of, composed of ….

examples.chinese: 我们班由三十个学生组成。
examples.english: Our class is made up of thirty students.

lessons.title: X也不是，Y也不是
lessons.explanation: Neither X nor Y feels right: caught in an awkward dilemma.

examples.chinese: 他站在门口，进也不是，退也不是。
examples.english: He stood at the door: going in felt wrong, and so did backing out.

lessons.title: X也X不得，Y也Y不得
lessons.explanation: Can neither do X nor do Y: nothing is permissible.

examples.chinese: 这孩子被惯坏了，说也说不得，碰也碰不得。
examples.english: The child is spoiled. You can neither scold him nor touch him.

lessons.title: X是它，Y也是它
lessons.explanation: It does X and it does Y too: one thing serves every purpose.

examples.chinese: 查资料是它，付钱也是它，手机什么都能做。
examples.english: It looks things up and it pays the bills: the phone does everything.

lessons.title: X着也是X着
lessons.explanation: Since it is idle anyway, might as well put it to use.

examples.chinese: 闲着也是闲着，我们把房间打扫一下吧。
examples.english: We are idle anyway. Let’s clean the room.

lessons.title: 不管怎样说
lessons.explanation: No matter what one says; in any case.

examples.chinese: 不管怎样说，他都是你的亲弟弟。
examples.english: No matter what, he is still your own younger brother.

lessons.title: 真有你/他/她的
lessons.explanation: You really are something! Admiring (or teasing) praise.

examples.chinese: 这么难的比赛你都赢了，真有你的！
examples.english: You even won such a difficult match. You really are something!

lessons.title: X什么X
lessons.explanation: V什么V: impatient rebuke, stop doing X!

examples.chinese: 哭什么哭，问题总能解决的。
examples.english: Stop crying: the problem can always be solved.

lessons.title: 什么X不X（的）
lessons.explanation: 什么X不X的: dismissing a concern as irrelevant.

examples.chinese: 什么贵不贵的，你喜欢就买。
examples.english: Never mind whether it is expensive: if you like it, buy it.

lessons.title: 不X白不X
lessons.explanation: If you don’t do X, it goes to waste: might as well do it.

examples.chinese: 这些水果是免费的，不吃白不吃。
examples.english: This fruit is free, not eating it would be a waste.

lessons.title: X来X去，都是/就是……
lessons.explanation: After going back and forth, it always comes down to ….

examples.chinese: 大家说来说去，都是那几个老问题。
examples.english: After all the back and forth, it was still the same old problems.

lessons.title: 动词+什么（就）是什么
lessons.explanation: Whatever one V-s counts: that person/thing decides.

examples.chinese: 这家小店没有菜单，老板做什么就是什么。
examples.english: This little shop has no menu: whatever the owner cooks is what you get.

lessons.title: 多项状语
lessons.explanation: Ordering multiple adverbials: time before place before manner.

examples.chinese: 他昨天在图书馆认真地复习了一天。
examples.english: Yesterday he reviewed earnestly in the library all day.

lessons.title: 可能补语“动词+得/不得”
lessons.explanation: V不得: the action must not / cannot be done.

examples.chinese: 学习是慢功夫，急不得。
examples.english: Learning takes time; you must not rush it.

lessons.title: 程度补语“形容词/心理动词+得+不得了”
lessons.pattern: 形容词/心理动词+得+不得了
lessons.explanation: Adj/psych-verb + 得不得了: to an extreme degree.

examples.chinese: 听说能去旅游，孩子们高兴得不得了。
examples.english: Hearing they could go traveling, the children were overjoyed.

lessons.title: 趋向补语的引申用法（下来/下去/起来/过来/过去）
lessons.pattern: 动词/形容词+下来/下去/起来/过来/过去
lessons.explanation: Directional complements extended to states, e.g. 下来 = settling into a state.

examples.chinese: 老师进来后，教室里安静下来。
examples.english: After the teacher came in, the classroom quieted down.

lessons.title: 状态补语“动词/形容词+得+短语”
lessons.pattern: 动词/形容词+得+动词短语/主谓短语/固定短语
lessons.explanation: V/Adj + 得 + phrase describing the resulting state.

examples.chinese: 他忙得连饭都忘了吃。
examples.english: He was so busy that he even forgot to eat.

lessons.title: “有”字句3
lessons.pattern: 主语+有+着+宾语；主语+动词+有+宾语
lessons.explanation: 有着 expressing possession/existence with emphasis; V+有 for attachment.

examples.chinese: 这座城市有着一千多年的历史。
examples.english: This city has a history of more than a thousand years.

lessons.title: “把”字句3
lessons.pattern: 主语+把+宾语+一+动词；主语+把+宾语1+动词+宾语2
lessons.explanation: 把-sentence with 一+V for abrupt action, or with a second object.

examples.chinese: 他把书包一放，就跑出去玩了。
examples.english: He plunked down his schoolbag and ran out to play.

lessons.title: 连动句3
lessons.pattern: 动词短语1+动词短语2（因果/转折/条件关系）
lessons.explanation: Serial-verb sentence where the two verb phrases are linked by cause, contrast or condition.

examples.chinese: 大家听了这个笑话都笑了。
examples.english: Everyone laughed on hearing this joke.

lessons.title: 比较句4
lessons.explanation: Comparison without 比: A Adj B by amount, e.g. 大我三岁.

examples.chinese: 姐姐大我三岁，从小就照顾我。
examples.english: My older sister is three years older than me and has looked after me since childhood.

lessons.title: 被动句3
lessons.pattern: 主语+被/叫/让+宾语+给+动词+其他成分
lessons.explanation: Passive with 被/叫/让 … 给 before the verb.

examples.chinese: 我的自行车叫弟弟给骑走了。
examples.english: My bike was ridden off by my younger brother.

lessons.title: 承接复句“……，便……”
lessons.explanation: Sequential clauses linked by 便 (then).

examples.chinese: 他下了课，便急急忙忙赶回家了。
examples.english: As soon as class ended, he hurried home.

lessons.title: 选择复句“或是……，或是……”
lessons.explanation: Alternative clauses: either … or ….

examples.chinese: 周末他或是看书，或是去爬山。
examples.english: On weekends he either reads or goes hiking.

lessons.title: 假设复句“一旦……，就……”
lessons.explanation: Once … happens, then ….

examples.chinese: 一旦下定决心，就不要轻易放弃。
examples.english: Once you have made up your mind, do not give up lightly.

lessons.title: 假设复句“假如……，（就）……”
lessons.explanation: If … (hypothetical), then ….

examples.chinese: 假如明天不下雨，我们就去公园。
examples.english: If it does not rain tomorrow, we will go to the park.

lessons.title: 假设复句“万一……，（就）……”
lessons.explanation: In case … (unlikely bad event), then ….

examples.chinese: 万一路上堵车，你就打车来吧。
examples.english: In case there is a traffic jam, just take a taxi.

lessons.title: 假设复句“……，要不然/不然……”
lessons.explanation: … otherwise ….

examples.chinese: 快点儿出发吧，要不然就赶不上火车了。
examples.english: Let’s set off quickly, otherwise we will miss the train.

lessons.title: 因果复句“……，因而……”
lessons.explanation: … and as a result / therefore ….

examples.chinese: 他平时练习很多，因而进步很快。
examples.english: He practices a lot, and therefore improves quickly.

lessons.title: 因果复句“……，可见……”
lessons.explanation: … from which one can see that ….

examples.chinese: 他连周末都在学习，可见有多努力。
examples.english: He studies even on weekends. You can see how hard-working he is.

lessons.title: 让步复句“哪怕……，也……”
lessons.explanation: Even if …, still ….

examples.chinese: 哪怕只有一点儿希望，我们也要努力。
examples.english: Even if there is only a little hope, we must still try hard.

lessons.title: 递进复句“不但不/不但没有……，反而……”
lessons.explanation: Not only not …, but on the contrary ….

examples.chinese: 吃了药，病不但没有好，反而更重了。
examples.english: After taking the medicine, the illness not only did not improve but got worse.

lessons.title: 递进复句“不是……，还/还是……”
lessons.explanation: Instead of …, (even) went further and ….

examples.chinese: 他不是来帮忙，还给大家添了不少麻烦。
examples.english: Instead of coming to help, he caused everyone a lot of trouble.

lessons.title: 目的复句“……，为的是……”
lessons.explanation: … for the purpose of ….

examples.chinese: 他每天早起跑步，为的是身体健康。
examples.english: He gets up early to run every day for the sake of his health.

lessons.title: 紧缩复句“没有……就没有……”
lessons.explanation: Without … there would be no ….

examples.chinese: 没有大家的帮助，就没有我今天的成绩。
examples.english: Without everyone’s help, I would not have today’s results.

lessons.title: 紧缩复句“不……不……”
lessons.explanation: Condensed conditional: if not …, then not ….

examples.chinese: 他不做完作业不睡觉。
examples.english: He will not sleep until he finishes his homework.

lessons.title: 紧缩复句“再……也……”
lessons.explanation: No matter how …, still ….

examples.chinese: 天气再热，他也不开空调。
examples.english: No matter how hot it gets, he still will not turn on the air conditioner.

lessons.title: 类前缀“超-、多-、反-、无-、亚-、准-”
lessons.explanation: Productive prefixes; 超- = super-, ultra-.

examples.chinese: 这家店专卖超低价的日用品。
examples.english: This shop specializes in ultra-low-priced daily goods.

lessons.title: 类后缀“-化、-式、-型、-性”
lessons.explanation: Productive suffixes; -化 = -ize/-ification.

examples.chinese: 近几年，农村的生活越来越现代化了。
examples.english: In recent years, rural life has become more and more modernized.

lessons.title: 人称代词“人家”
lessons.explanation: 人家: others / that person / I (coy self-reference).

examples.chinese: 人家都开始复习了，你还在玩。
examples.english: Everyone else has started reviewing, and you are still playing.

lessons.title: 名量词“串、滴、枝、扇、卷”
lessons.explanation: Level-6 nominal measure words; 串 = a string/bunch of.

examples.chinese: 他买了一串葡萄和两串香蕉。
examples.english: He bought a bunch of grapes and two bunches of bananas.

lessons.title: 动量词“番”
lessons.explanation: Verbal measure word 番: a round/bout of effortful action.

examples.chinese: 经过一番努力，他终于考上了大学。
examples.english: After a good deal of effort, he finally got into university.

lessons.title: 程度副词“特、异常、较为”
lessons.explanation: Degree adverbs; 异常 = unusually, exceptionally.

examples.chinese: 听到这个消息，他显得异常激动。
examples.english: On hearing the news, he seemed unusually agitated.

lessons.title: 范围副词“净、一同、大都”
lessons.explanation: Scope adverbs; 净 = nothing but, only.

examples.chinese: 你怎么净说些让人生气的话？
examples.english: Why do you say nothing but infuriating things?

lessons.title: 时间副词“一时、不时、仍旧、依旧、一向”
lessons.explanation: Time adverbs; 依旧 = still, as before.

examples.chinese: 十年过去了，小镇依旧那么安静。
examples.english: Ten years on, the small town is as quiet as ever.

lessons.title: 频率副词“一再、再三”
lessons.explanation: Frequency adverbs; 再三 = again and again, repeatedly.

examples.chinese: 出门前，妈妈再三提醒我带伞。
examples.english: Before I left, Mom reminded me again and again to take an umbrella.

lessons.title: 方式副词“不禁、赶忙、特地、特意、偷偷”
lessons.explanation: Manner adverbs; 不禁 = cannot help but.

examples.chinese: 看到儿时的照片，她不禁笑了。
examples.english: Seeing her childhood photos, she could not help smiling.

lessons.title: 否定副词“未必”
lessons.explanation: 未必: not necessarily.

examples.chinese: 贵的东西未必就是好的。
examples.english: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

lessons.title: 语气副词“恰好、倒是、干脆、明明、总算”
lessons.explanation: Tone adverbs; 明明 = clearly, obviously (contradicting).

examples.chinese: 你明明知道答案，为什么不说？
examples.english: You clearly know the answer. Why not say it?

lessons.title: 介词“于”（引出时间、处所）
lessons.explanation: Formal preposition 于: at/in/on (time or place).

examples.chinese: 这座大桥建于上个世纪五十年代。
examples.english: This bridge was built in the 1950s.

lessons.title: 介词“至于”（引出对象）
lessons.explanation: 至于: as for, as to (shifting topic).

examples.chinese: 我先报名，至于去不去，以后再说。
examples.english: I will sign up first; as for whether I go, we will see later.

lessons.title: 介词“因”（引出目的、原因）
lessons.explanation: Formal preposition 因: because of, due to.

examples.chinese: 航班因大雾推迟了两个小时。
examples.english: The flight was delayed two hours due to heavy fog.

lessons.title: 介词“除”（表示排除）
lessons.explanation: 除 (…外/之外): except for, apart from.

examples.chinese: 除周末外，他每天都去健身房。
examples.english: Except on weekends, he goes to the gym every day.

lessons.title: 连词“不料”（连接分句或句子）
lessons.explanation: 不料: unexpectedly, who would have thought.

examples.chinese: 我以为他会答应，不料他一口拒绝了。
examples.english: I thought he would agree; unexpectedly, he refused outright.

lessons.title: 结构助词“所”
lessons.explanation: Structural particle 所 before a verb forming a nominal: that which is V-ed.

examples.chinese: 他所说的一切后来都得到了证实。
examples.english: Everything he said was later confirmed.

lessons.title: 语气助词“啦、嘛”
lessons.explanation: Sentence-final particles; 嘛 marks obviousness or mild urging.

examples.chinese: 有意见就直接提嘛，别放在心里。
examples.english: If you have objections, just raise them: don’t keep them inside.

lessons.title: 其他助词“也好”
lessons.explanation: X也好，Y也好: whether X or Y, it makes no difference.

examples.chinese: 同意也好，反对也好，请先听我说完。
examples.english: Whether you agree or object, please hear me out first.

lessons.title: 四字格“A这A那”
lessons.explanation: V这V那: fussily doing the action to this and that.

examples.chinese: 她买衣服总是挑这挑那，半天定不下来。
examples.english: When buying clothes she picks at this and that and cannot decide for ages.

lessons.title: 四字格“左A右B”
lessons.explanation: 左A右B: doing the action repeatedly from all sides, e.g. 左思右想.

examples.chinese: 他左思右想，还是觉得这事不对劲。
examples.english: He turned it over and over in his mind and still felt something was off.

lessons.title: 固定短语“好（不）容易”
lessons.explanation: 好（不）容易: only with great difficulty (both forms mean the same).

examples.chinese: 我排了两个小时队，好不容易才买到票。
examples.english: I queued for two hours and finally managed to buy a ticket.

lessons.title: 固定短语“那倒（也）是”
lessons.explanation: 那倒（也）是: “that’s true, actually”, conceding a point.

examples.chinese: “坐高铁比开车快多了。”“那倒是。”
examples.english: “Taking the high-speed train is much faster than driving.” “That’s true.”

lessons.title: 固定短语“算了”
lessons.explanation: 算了: forget it, let it go.

examples.chinese: 他不愿意去就算了，咱们别勉强。
examples.english: If he does not want to go, forget it. Let’s not force him.

lessons.title: 固定短语“得了”
lessons.explanation: Sentence-final 得了: just do X and be done with it.

examples.chinese: 别纠结了，就买这件得了。
examples.english: Stop agonizing, just buy this one and be done with it.

lessons.title: A一+量词，B一+量词
lessons.explanation: One from A, one from B: many people chiming in by turns.

examples.chinese: 会上大家你一句，我一句，讨论得十分热烈。
examples.english: At the meeting everyone chimed in one after another, and the discussion was lively.

lessons.title: 东一A，西一A
lessons.explanation: One here, one there: scattered in disorder.

examples.chinese: 屋里衣服东一件，西一件，乱得下不去脚。
examples.english: Clothes lay scattered here and there in the room; there was nowhere to step.

lessons.title: 到……为止
lessons.explanation: Up until …; ending at ….

examples.chinese: 到目前为止，报名的人已经超过一百了。
examples.english: Up to now, more than a hundred people have signed up.

lessons.title: X到Y头上来了
lessons.explanation: The trouble/action has come down on Y’s head.

examples.chinese: 他居然把主意打到我头上来了。
examples.english: He actually set his sights on me.

lessons.title: 不X不……，一X……
lessons.explanation: You don’t know until you X, and when you do, it’s a shock.

examples.chinese: 不看不知道，一看吓一跳，这个月竟花了一万块。
examples.english: I had no idea until I looked, and what a shock: ten thousand yuan spent this month.

lessons.title: 好你个X
lessons.explanation: Why, you …! Mock-angry exclamation at someone.

examples.chinese: 好你个小张，偷偷把我的零食吃光了！
examples.english: Why, you little Zhang. You secretly ate up all my snacks!

lessons.title: 早（也）不X，晚（也）不X
lessons.explanation: Of all times, it had to happen right now.

examples.chinese: 电梯早不坏，晚不坏，偏偏上班时坏了。
examples.english: The elevator did not break earlier or later. It had to break right at rush hour.

lessons.title: 看/瞧+把+宾语（施事）+X得
lessons.explanation: Look how X-ed you are! Teasing comment on someone’s state.

examples.chinese: 瞧把你高兴得，不就是赢了一盘棋吗？
examples.english: Look how pleased you are. It was only one game of chess!

lessons.title: 放着X不Y
lessons.explanation: To leave the obvious good option X aside and not do Y with it.

examples.chinese: 放着近路不走，你偏要绕远。
examples.english: With a shortcut right there, you insist on going the long way.

lessons.title: X了就X了，（没）有……
lessons.explanation: What’s done is done: no use dwelling on it.

examples.chinese: 杯子碎了就碎了，没有什么大不了的。
examples.english: The cup is broken, so be it; it is no big deal.

lessons.title: 这/那也不X，那/这也不Y
lessons.explanation: Unhappy with this and that alike: impossible to please.

examples.chinese: 他这也不吃，那也不吃，真难伺候。
examples.english: He will not eat this and will not eat that, so hard to please.

lessons.title: X归X，Y归Y
lessons.explanation: X is one thing, Y is another: keep them separate.

examples.chinese: 工作归工作，生活归生活，得分开。
examples.english: Work is work and life is life. They must be kept apart.

lessons.title: 看你X的/瞧他X的
lessons.explanation: Look at you, all X! Teasing or deflecting remark.

examples.chinese: 看你急的，先坐下喝口水慢慢说。
examples.english: Look how worked up you are: sit down, have some water, and tell me slowly.

lessons.title: 程度补语“动词/形容词+透+了”
lessons.explanation: V/Adj + 透了: thoroughly, to the utmost (usually negative).

examples.chinese: 连着加了一个星期班，他烦透了。
examples.english: After a whole week of overtime, he was utterly fed up.

lessons.title: “把”字句4
lessons.pattern: 主语（非生物体）+把+宾语+动词+其他成分；主语+把+宾语（施事）+动词+其他成分
lessons.explanation: 把-sentence with an inanimate subject, or whose object is the agent of the result.

examples.chinese: 一场大风把院子里的花全刮倒了。
examples.english: A strong wind blew down all the flowers in the yard.

lessons.title: 并列复句“一时……一时……”
lessons.explanation: Now …, now …: alternating states.

examples.chinese: 山里的天气一时晴，一时雨，说变就变。
examples.english: The mountain weather is now sunny, now rainy. It changes in an instant.

lessons.title: 选择复句“要么……，要么……”
lessons.explanation: Either … or … (exclusive choice).

examples.chinese: 周末他要么在家看书，要么去郊外爬山。
examples.english: On weekends he either reads at home or hikes in the outskirts.

lessons.title: 转折复句“虽……，但/可/却/也……”
lessons.explanation: Although … (written 虽), yet ….

examples.chinese: 房间虽小，却收拾得干净整齐。
examples.english: Though the room is small, it is kept clean and tidy.

lessons.title: 条件复句“凡是……，都……”
lessons.explanation: All that … invariably ….

examples.chinese: 凡是他答应过的事，都会做到。
examples.english: Whatever he has promised, he will do.

lessons.title: 条件复句“除非……，才……”
lessons.explanation: Only if … will ….

examples.chinese: 除非亲眼看见，他才肯相信。
examples.english: Only if he sees it with his own eyes will he believe it.

lessons.title: 条件复句“除非……，否则/不然……”
lessons.explanation: Unless …, otherwise ….

examples.chinese: 除非提前预订，否则周末根本没有位子。
examples.english: Unless you book ahead, there are simply no seats on weekends.

lessons.title: 让步复句“就算……，也……”
lessons.explanation: Even if …, still ….

examples.chinese: 就算再忙，也要按时吃饭。
examples.english: Even at your busiest, you should still eat on time.

lessons.title: 目的复句“……，以便……”
lessons.explanation: … so as to, in order to (facilitate) ….

examples.chinese: 请留下电话号码，以便我们及时联系您。
examples.english: Please leave your phone number so that we can contact you promptly.

lessons.title: 类前缀"后-、亲-"
lessons.explanation: Prefix-like morphemes: 后- "post-" (后疫情) and 亲- "pro-" (亲环境) coin new nouns and adjectives.

examples.chinese: 后疫情时代，远程办公已成为常态。
examples.english: In the post-pandemic era, remote work has become the norm.

lessons.title: 类后缀"-观、-鬼、-界、-然、-坛、-为、-制"
lessons.explanation: Suffix-like morphemes productively form abstract nouns: 价值观, 学术界, 体坛, 终身制, 胆小鬼.

examples.chinese: 这一发现震动了整个学术界。
examples.english: This discovery shook the entire academic world.

lessons.title: 动词"恨不得/巴不得"
lessons.pattern: 恨不得/巴不得+动词短语
lessons.explanation: Expresses an intense, often unrealizable eagerness: "to itch to, to wish one could".

examples.chinese: 他恨不得立刻飞回家乡看望母亲。
examples.english: He wished he could fly home at once to see his mother.

lessons.title: 动词"免不了/犯不着/犯得着"
lessons.explanation: 免不了 "cannot avoid"; 犯不着/犯得着 "not worth / worth the trouble of".

examples.chinese: 为这点小事生气，实在犯不着。
examples.english: It is really not worth getting angry over such a trifle.

lessons.title: 动词"并非"
lessons.explanation: Formal emphatic negation: "is by no means, is not at all".

examples.chinese: 成功并非偶然，而是长期积累的结果。
examples.english: Success is by no means accidental; it is the fruit of long accumulation.

lessons.title: 动词"可谓"
lessons.explanation: Formal evaluative verb: "may well be called, can be described as".

examples.chinese: 这场演出可谓精彩绝伦。
examples.english: This performance can well be called spectacular.

lessons.title: 动词"所谓"
lessons.explanation: "So-called": quotes or distances the speaker from a label.

examples.chinese: 那些所谓的捷径往往暗藏风险。
examples.english: Those so-called shortcuts often conceal risks.

lessons.title: 动词"有所"
lessons.explanation: Formal "to some extent": 有所 + bisyllabic verb marks measured change.

examples.chinese: 与去年相比，公司业绩有所增长。
examples.english: Compared with last year, company performance has grown somewhat.

lessons.title: 动词"予以"
lessons.explanation: Formal "to give, to grant (a treatment)": common in official writing.

examples.chinese: 对违规行为，监管部门将予以处罚。
examples.english: Regulators will impose penalties on violations.

lessons.title: 动词"可否"
lessons.explanation: Formal "whether or not it is possible", often in polite requests.

examples.chinese: 可否请您再详细说明一下？
examples.english: Might I ask you to explain in a little more detail?

lessons.title: 动词"除外"
lessons.explanation: "Excepted, excluded": placed after the item that is excluded.

examples.chinese: 展馆全年开放，法定节假日除外。
examples.english: The hall is open year-round, statutory holidays excepted.

lessons.title: 文言代词"何/彼/兹"
lessons.explanation: Literary pronouns: 何 "what/why", 彼 "that/the other", 兹 "this", formal written register.

examples.chinese: 此事该从何说起，他一时语塞。
examples.english: Where to even begin with this. He was momentarily at a loss.

lessons.title: 代词"这么着/怎么着"
lessons.explanation: Colloquial pro-forms standing in for a manner or action: "like this / do what".

examples.chinese: 你到底想怎么着，痛快点说吧。
examples.english: What exactly do you want? Out with it.

lessons.title: 数量代词"若干"
lessons.explanation: Formal indefinite quantity: "a certain number of, several".

examples.chinese: 报告最后提出了若干条建议。
examples.english: The report closes with a number of recommendations.

lessons.title: 名量词：重、截、缕、码、枚、摊、丸、则、幢、宗
lessons.explanation: Advanced nominal classifiers; 枚 counts small objects such as coins, medals, stamps.

examples.chinese: 她在世锦赛上摘得两枚金牌。
examples.english: She took two gold medals at the world championships.

lessons.title: 动量词"通"
lessons.explanation: Verbal classifier for a bout of scolding, phoning, drumming, etc.

examples.chinese: 他把儿子狠狠训了一通。
examples.english: He gave his son a good telling-off.

lessons.title: 复合量词"人次"
lessons.explanation: Compound classifier "person-times", counting cumulative visits or uses.

examples.chinese: 该展览累计接待观众逾百万人次。
examples.english: The exhibition has received over a million visits in total.

lessons.title: 程度副词：尤为、分外、颇、愈加、越发等
lessons.explanation: Written-register degree adverbs: 尤为 "especially", 颇 "quite", 愈加/越发 "increasingly".

examples.chinese: 在众多参赛作品中，这一幅尤为出色。
examples.english: Among the many entries, this one is especially outstanding.

lessons.title: 范围副词：皆、均、唯、统统、一概等
lessons.explanation: Formal scope adverbs: 均/皆 "all without exception", 唯 "only", 一概 "categorically".

examples.chinese: 双方均对谈判结果表示满意。
examples.english: Both sides expressed satisfaction with the outcome of the talks.

lessons.title: 时间副词：届时、尚、随即、历来、一经等
lessons.explanation: Formal time adverbs: 届时 "at that (future) time", 尚 "still", 随即 "right after".

examples.chinese: 决赛下月举行，届时强手云集。
examples.english: The final is next month; strong contenders will gather then.

lessons.title: 频率副词：屡次、屡屡、时而、相继、再度等
lessons.explanation: Frequency adverbs of formal register: 屡次/屡屡 "repeatedly", 相继 "one after another", 再度 "once again".

examples.chinese: 他屡次打破全国纪录。
examples.english: He has repeatedly broken the national record.

lessons.title: 方式副词：毅然、擅自、竭力、骤然、逐一等
lessons.explanation: Manner adverbs: 毅然 "resolutely", 擅自 "without authorization", 竭力 "with all one’s might".

examples.chinese: 他放弃高薪，毅然回乡创业。
examples.english: He gave up a high salary and resolutely went home to start a business.

lessons.title: 否定副词：不见得、绝不、无从、无须、勿
lessons.explanation: Negation adverbs: 无从 "have no way to", 无须 "need not", 勿 "do not (literary)".

examples.chinese: 年代久远，传闻已无从考证。
examples.english: So long ago, the rumor can no longer be verified.

lessons.title: 语气副词：不妨、索性、势必、未免、偏偏等
lessons.explanation: Modal adverbs: 索性 "might as well, simply", 不妨 "no harm in", 势必 "be bound to".

examples.chinese: 既然睡不着，他索性起身看书。
examples.english: Unable to sleep, he simply got up to read.

lessons.title: 语气副词"何必/何尝/何不/何苦"
lessons.explanation: Rhetorical 何-series adverbs: 何必 "why bother", 何尝 "when ever did", 何苦 "why go to the trouble".

examples.chinese: 都是多年同事，何必斤斤计较？
examples.english: You are colleagues of many years. Why haggle over trifles?
